practices.name: Listening to the inner sound (VBT verses 38-39)
practices.howto: Sit comfortably and let the breath settle by itself. Listen for a faint inner sound, a soft ringing or hum beneath the sounds of the room. Rest attention on it lightly, without straining to hear. Let it be loud, soft, present or absent; do not follow it into images or stories. When the mind wanders, come back to listening. If the sound fades into quiet, rest in the quiet. When you finish, notice the ordinary sounds around you again.
practices.source_note: Vijñāna Bhairava verses 38-39 (nāda-yoga), tr. Christopher Hareesh Wallis (Tantra 112 full text) and his blog post on these verses. Satsang summary in its own words.
contraindications: If you live with tinnitus that distresses you, listen instead to an outer sound such as a bell or a held note as it fades (verses 40-41).
If you feel disoriented, unreal or anxious, open the eyes, feel the feet and the seat, and stop for today.

practices.name: The body as awareness (VBT verse 63)
practices.howto: Sit and let attention rest on the whole body at once: not one part, the whole field of sensation. Then take the body, and the world around it, as made of awareness. Let this be felt rather than thought. When the mind narrows back to "me" and "mine", return to the wider field and rest there. The body stays where it is; only the sense of it being separate softens.
practices.source_note: Vijñāna Bhairava verse 63, tr. Christopher Hareesh Wallis (Tantra 112 full text). Satsang summary in its own words.
contraindications: If you feel disoriented, unreal or anxious, open the eyes, feel the feet and the seat, and stop for today.
If you have a history of trauma, dissociation, psychosis or severe anxiety, keep sits short with eyes open, or practise with a qualified teacher or clinician.

practices.name: Resting between objects (VBT verse 62)
practices.howto: First settle with the breath for a few minutes. Then notice the moment the mind lets go of one thing, a sensation, a thought, a sound, and before it takes up the next. Rest in that in-between. Do not chase the next object and do not push it away. When you find you have already moved on, come back to the gap. Practise the breath-pause sit first; this one needs a little steadiness.
practices.source_note: Vijñāna Bhairava verse 62 (with 61), tr. Christopher Hareesh Wallis (Tantra 112 full text). Satsang summary in its own words.

practices.name: Spaciousness: a wall of skin with nothing inside (VBT verses 43-48)
practices.howto: Sit and notice the space of the room around you, the space that holds the walls and your body. Then sense the space inside the body: the chest, the mouth, the skull. Feel the skin as a thin wall with open space within and without. Let the inner and outer space be one field and rest in that openness. When the mind reaches for something solid, notice the reaching and return to space. Stay alert; this is not a blank or sleepy state.

practices.name: Touching the end-of-twelve through the day (VBT verse 51)
practices.howto: This is a daily-life practice, not a sit. Several times a day, while walking, waiting or eating, let attention rest for a few breaths at the space just above the crown of the head, the "end of twelve", then carry on with what you were doing. Keep the touch light and brief. The remembering is the practice.
practices.source_note: Vijñāna Bhairava verse 51 (the end-of-twelve, dvādaśānta, "however and wherever" through the day), tr. Christopher Hareesh Wallis (Tantra 112 full text) and his blog post on verses 49-51. The pack read "the twelve" as twelve body centres; the verse names one place, the end-of-twelve. Satsang summary in its own words.
contraindications: If attention above the head brings headache, pressure or dizziness, rest it in the heart or the soles of the feet instead.
If you feel disoriented, unreal or anxious, open the eyes, feel the feet and the seat, and stop for today.

practices.name: Merging the sense spaces (VBT verses 32-33)
practices.howto: Sit and bring attention to one sense contact: a sound, a touch, something seen. Notice the outer space where it arrives, the room and the distance. Then notice the inner space where it is received. Rest in both at once, the outer and the inner as one field with the sensation in the middle. When attention falls to one side, come back to both.
